questions.stem: Which organ excretes carbon dioxide from the human body?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide produced by respiration in the cells is carried in the plasma to the lungs, where it diffuses across the alveolar walls into the air and is breathed out. Water vapour leaves by the same route.

distractorRationale.a: The kidney excretes urea, excess water and salts in urine
distractorRationale.c: The liver makes urea and excretes bile pigments, but not carbon dioxide
distractorRationale.d: The large intestine reabsorbs water and passes out faeces, which is egestion

options.text: liver, by deamination of excess amino acids
stomach, by the action of pepsin

questions.explanation: Amino acids that the body does not need cannot be stored, so the liver strips off the amino group, producing highly toxic ammonia, which is immediately converted to the much safer urea. The kidney then removes that urea from the blood, but it does not manufacture it.

distractorRationale.a: The kidney filters urea out of the blood; formation happens in the liver
distractorRationale.c: Pepsin digests protein into peptides and forms no urea
distractorRationale.d: The bladder simply stores urine that already contains urea

questions.stem: Why is the passing out of faeces described as egestion rather than excretion?

options.text: Because faeces is undigested food that was never absorbed into the cells, so it is not a product of metabolism
Because faeces leaves through the anus

questions.explanation: Excretion refers specifically to substances produced by the body's own chemical reactions, such as urea and carbon dioxide. Faeces is mainly undigested cellulose, dead cells and bacteria that passed through the gut without entering the body's metabolism, so its removal is egestion.

distractorRationale.a: Urine also contains water and is nevertheless excretory
distractorRationale.c: The route out of the body does not determine the classification
distractorRationale.d: The presence of bacteria is incidental to the definition

questions.stem: The excretory structure of an earthworm is the
questions.explanation: An earthworm has a pair of nephridia in almost every segment. Each is a coiled tubule that collects waste from the body fluid and discharges it through a pore in the body wall, an arrangement suited to a segmented body.

distractorRationale.a: Contractile vacuoles occur in single-celled protists such as Amoeba and Paramecium
distractorRationale.c: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects
distractorRationale.d: Flame cells are found in flatworms such as the tapeworm and planarian

questions.stem: Insects and birds excrete nitrogenous waste as uric acid rather than as urea. The main advantage of this is that uric acid

options.text: is more toxic, so less is needed
is almost insoluble, so very little water is lost in removing it

questions.explanation: Uric acid can be excreted as a near-dry paste, so almost no water is sacrificed. That matters enormously for a flying bird carrying no spare weight and for a developing egg with a fixed water supply sealed inside the shell.

distractorRationale.a: Uric acid is less toxic than ammonia, and greater toxicity would be a disadvantage
distractorRationale.c: Excretory products are wastes and yield no useful energy on removal
distractorRationale.d: Its low solubility is precisely the property that saves water

questions.stem: Which of the following is an excretory product of a flowering plant?

options.text: Oxygen released through the stomata during the day

questions.explanation: Oxygen is produced by photosynthesis in excess of what the plant needs for respiration, so the surplus diffuses out through the stomata as a genuine waste product. Plants also excrete carbon dioxide, water vapour and stored substances such as tannins and latex.

distractorRationale.a: Plants do not produce urea; they reuse nitrogen rather than excreting it
distractorRationale.c: Starch is a stored food reserve, deliberately kept, not a waste
distractorRationale.d: Sucrose is a useful food being transported to where it is needed

questions.stem: Sweat produced by the skin contains water, mineral salts and a small quantity of
questions.explanation: Sweat is a dilute solution of sodium chloride and other salts in water, with a trace of urea, which is why the skin counts as a minor excretory organ. Its main role, however, is cooling the body as the water evaporates.

distractorRationale.b: Glucose is a valuable nutrient and is reabsorbed rather than excreted; glucose in sweat or urine suggests diabetes
distractorRationale.c: Protein molecules are too large to be secreted in sweat
distractorRationale.d: Bile pigments leave in bile through the gut, not through the skin

questions.stem: The secretion of saliva by the salivary glands is an example of excretion.
questions.explanation: False. Saliva is manufactured deliberately for a purpose — it moistens food and supplies salivary amylase — so releasing it is secretion. Excretion removes substances the body must get rid of, such as urea and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: How does Amoeba get rid of the excess water that continually enters its body?

options.text: Through a contractile vacuole that fills and then discharges at the surface
Through Malpighian tubules attached to the gut
Through stomata in the cell membrane

questions.explanation: Amoeba lives in fresh water, which is more dilute than its cytoplasm, so water enters constantly by osmosis. A contractile vacuole collects this surplus water and then contracts to expel it at the cell surface, preventing the cell from bursting.

distractorRationale.b: Nephridia are the excretory organs of segmented worms such as the earthworm
distractorRationale.c: Malpighian tubules belong to insects, which have a gut
distractorRationale.d: Stomata are pores in plant leaves and stems, not in cell membranes

questions.stem: Distinguish between excretion, egestion and secretion, giving one example of each. Then name the four excretory organs of a mammal and state one product removed by each.
markingGuide: Excretion defined as the removal of the waste products of metabolism, with a valid example such as urea in urine or carbon dioxide from the lungs (2 marks)
Egestion defined as the removal of undigested food as faeces, which was never absorbed into the cells (2 marks)
Secretion defined as the release of a useful substance produced by a gland, with a valid example such as saliva, bile, insulin or enzymes (2 marks)
Kidney — urea, excess water and excess mineral salts (1 mark)
Lungs — carbon dioxide and water vapour (1 mark)
Skin — water, mineral salts and a trace of urea in sweat (1 mark)
Liver — bile pigments from the breakdown of haemoglobin (1 mark)
questions.explanation: The three definitions turn on the origin and usefulness of the substance: excretory products come from metabolism and are harmful, egested material never entered the cells, and secretions are made deliberately for a purpose. Each organ must be paired with a product that it genuinely removes.
